shape_hint: Cylindrical pin with a flat round head (diameter dk, height k, small fillet r under the head) and a small cross hole (diameter d1) near the free end for a split pin; pin end slightly chamfered (c). Type A has no hole, Type B has the hole at distance le from the head underside.

role_map.c_max: chamfer/end dimension c max at the pin end (per ISO 2341 figure)
role_map.e: dimension e at the hole/end (per ISO 2341 figure)
role_map.le_min: minimum distance from head underside to the hole (effective length le)

notes: Metric ISO 2341 / DIN 1444 only, d 4..24 (12 of 26 listed sizes). Pin length l series is not tabulated. INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT: fasteners.eu, boltport.com and ferrofast.com (+ boltsfastener.com) show the same typo on the sibling ISO 2340/DIN 1443 table, which suggests a common upstream; counted leniently as separate sources here (row_support 4: globalfastener, fasteners.eu, boltport, ferrofast/boltsfastener; 3 for c,e,r columns which ferrofast lacks). If those four are treated as ONE source the true independent support is 2 (globalfastener vs that group) - maintainer must decide. No other independent page with the numbers was reachable (Fuller has no DIN 1444 page; Muehl has none; lexikon has no data).

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched live (HTTP 200) gf 2341, fasteners.eu iso/2341 + din/1444, boltport din-1444, ferrofast iso-2341, boltsfastener din-1444, fasten.it din_1444 (+ sibling ISO 2340/DIN 1443 tables of fasteners.eu, boltport, ferrofast, boltsfastener, gf, fasten.it for the typo test). Matrix 12 rows (4..24) x 8 columns x 7 pages (+ rows 3, 27..100 on gf/fasten.it/ferrofast/boltsfastener). Result: dk and d1: all 12 rows 3 clusters (A,B,C), 0 conflicts; k: 10 rows 3 clusters, rows 22 (5.5 vs fasten.it 5) and 24 (6 vs fasten.it 6.3) only 2 clusters + 1 dissent -> dropped; r: A,B only (fasten.it/ferrofast/boltsfastener lack it) -> 2 clusters; c_max, e, le_min numerically 3 clusters for all 12 rows (0 conflicts) but dropped for semantics. Sanity: dk/d 1.5-1.8, k<dk, d1 = ISO 1234 split pin sizes, all non-decreasing.
problems: Strict reading (fasteners.eu+boltport+ferrofast+boltsfastener = one cluster) would leave only 2 clusters (gf vs group) as the producer feared; fasten.it DIN 1444 (not found by producer) is the third cluster for d, dk, d1, k, c, e, le.

Rows 22 and 24 dropped: k=5.5/6 (gf, group, ISO numbers) vs fasten.it 5/6.3 (DIN 1444:1974); same DIN/ISO split at d=27 (k 6 vs 6.3) and e at d=50 (2 vs 3). Dissent from a different edition leaves only 2 clusters on the ISO numbers.

c_max, e, le_min dropped (meaning not readable): fasteners.eu legend defines both 'c - taper' and 'e - taper' (indistinguishable); gf prints 'e ~' bare; le legend says 'le - distance from the axis of the hole to face' (and ISO 2340 'w - distance ... from the front of pin', same numbers) i.e. hole axis to PIN END, whereas the record/role_map says 'head underside to hole' -> record's le_min semantics are wrong, not just unclear.
r dropped: only gf, fasteners.eu, boltport list it (A + group = 2 clusters).

Header-mapping risk: ferrofast/boltsfastener use d1,d2,d3,k,w (not ISO symbols); mapping to d, dk, d1, k, le is by magnitude and by agreement with explicit-header pages; harmless for rows 4..24 (group has explicit pages) but it is the only group evidence for rows 3, 27, 30, 36.

Possible re-run additions (not in record, ignore for this verdict): rows 3 (dk 5, d1 0.8, k 1), 30 (44, 8, 8), 36 (50, 8, 8) have 3 clusters (gf, ferrofast/boltsfastener, fasten.it) for d, dk, d1, k; row 27 fails on k (6 vs 6.3).

Family mismatch: family 'clevis' = ISO 2341 (headed) + ISO 2340/DIN 1443 (headless) + ISO 8738/DIN 1440 washers + ASME B18.8.1 inch (sys=both); record covers ISO 2341/DIN 1444 headed metric only, d 4..24 (10 rows after drops of 26 sizes). Headless table exists on gf/fasten.it/fe/boltport/ferrofast but the group carries the c max=33 typo at d=12.
Kept-column semantics read from fasteners.eu legend: d - pin diameter (h11), dk - head diameter (h14), k - head height (js14), d1 - diameter of hole for cotter pin (H13).
